source: Minchat Shai on Gen 33:4 ('וישקהו — dotted with SIX dots, a dot on every letter: Bereshit Rabbah, Shir HaShirim Rabbah, the Zohar; Pirkei de-R. Eliezer: read not he-KISSED him but he-BIT him') + Kitzur ('dotted above — he meant to bite him')
claim_en: THE SIX-DOTTED KISS: וישקהו ('and he fell on his neck AND KISSED HIM, and they wept,' 33:4) — the fourth of the TEN DOTTED PLACES reached in canon order, and SNAPSHOT carries all SIX dots, one over each letter, exactly as Bereshit Rabbah counts them (DB-checked at the codepoint level): the tradition that reads the kiss as a bite riding letter by letter in the stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 33:4 ('צוארו — read צואריו per the Masorah; so Chizkuni; the Zohar carries a teaching on it')
claim_en: THE NECK WRITTEN ONE, READ MANY: צוארו ('he fell on his NECK,' 33:4) — the Masorah reads the plural ('his necks,' with yod); the letter writes the singular, no yod in the stream (DB-checked): a written/read split carried here as a single written-form token — unlike the two-token encoding at 8:17, the instrument varying by site as previously characterized.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 33:14 ('שעירה — three in the Masorah: to-my-lord-to-Seir, Esau-returned-to-Seir, the-bare-mountain-rising-to-Seir (Joshua); and the FINAL letters of until-I-come-to-my-lord-to-Seir spell אליה — he will come to him after the four exiles, before the great day, when the saviors ascend Mount Zion to judge Esau's mountain')
claim_en: ELIJAH IN THE FINALS OF THE SEIR PROMISE: אבא אל אדני שעירה ('until I COME to my lord, to Seir,' 33:14 — the visit Jacob never pays in his lifetime) — the four words' final letters spell אליה (Elijah, DB-checked in order): the Kitzur reads the deferred arrival as the end of days, when the saviors ascend Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau (Obadiah, named). And the place-word itself stands exactly twice in the Torah, both in this meeting (33:14, 33:16, builder-checked), the Joshua member outside.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 33:1 ('וירא והנה — with GALGAL, not with maqqef; so Ben Asher's variant-lists') + 33:10 ('כי על כן — כי with GALGAL, not with maqqef')
claim_en: THE WHEEL-ACCENT'S TWO STATIONS: at the lifting of the eyes ('and he saw, AND BEHOLD, Esau coming,' 33:1) and at the gift-plea ('FOR therefore I have seen your face,' 33:10) Minchat Shai rules galgal (the wheel-accent), not maqqef — and SNAPSHOT carries NO maqqef at either station exactly as ruled (DB-checked), but stores the munach stroke where the wheel should turn: the galgal-vs-munach variance class grows to three stations (with 29:27), the layer's second and third source-anchored members.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 33:5 ('אלה לך — the lamed DAGESHED')
claim_en: WHO ARE THESE TO YOU — THE JOINED DAGESH: לך ('who are these TO YOU?', 33:5 — Esau over the children) — the lamed dageshed exactly as ruled, the joining dot after the open vowel binding the question to its object.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 33:8 ('פגשתי — the gimel in QAMATZ in the precise manuscripts and old prints; so Or Torah, against the printer's emendation')
claim_en: I-HAVE-MET IN QAMATZ: פגשתי ('all this camp that I MET,' 33:8) — the gimel in qamatz (the long a) with the precise manuscripts and Or Torah against the printer's emendation, at the pause of the etnachta.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 33:8 ('מי לך — three in the Masorah: who-is-to-you this whole camp; who-is-to-you here, that you hewed a tomb (Isa 22:16); who-else-is-to-you here — Lot at Sodom: the angel-companies striking Esau's men until they hewed graves') + MS 33:12 ('לנגדך — the gimel soft') + Kitzur 33:12 (the pair with Ps 90:8: 'why walk beside me and remember my sins BEFORE YOU')
claim_en: WHO-IS-TO-YOU, TWICE IN THE TORAH: the question-pair מי לך stands exactly twice — the angel at Sodom to Lot ('WHO else is TO YOU here?', 19:12) and Jacob's meeting ('WHO is all this camp TO YOU?', 33:8, builder-checked), the tomb-hewer of Isaiah named third; and Esau's offered escort is declined in a soft letter — לנגדך ('let me go BESIDE YOU,' 33:12) with the gimel soft as ruled, the word itself Torah-unique, its Masorah partner the psalm's 'our sins set BEFORE YOU' (Ps 90:8, named) — the Kitzur hearing Jacob's refusal inside it.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 33:13 ('הילדים — every the-children in Scripture: the he WITHOUT the stress-stroke; the Michlol')
claim_en: THE CHILDREN'S UNSTROKED HE: הילדים ('my lord knows that THE CHILDREN are tender,' 33:13) — the Michlol's rule that the-children never takes the stress-stroke on its he holds across all seven Torah tokens (builder-checked, five of them in this unit; the midwives' two at Exodus 1 carry only the verse-end stroke): the tender ones carried lightly in the pointing itself.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 33:10 ('כראת פני אלהים — PROFANE, tractate Soferim ch. 4') + Kitzur ('the count of the words equals your-prince: he hinted — I saw your angel and was saved')
claim_en: THE PROFANE SIGHT (classification layer, uninstrumented): 'for I have seen your face AS ONE SEES THE FACE OF אלהים' (33:10) — tractate Soferim rules this Name PROFANE (a great one's face, Esau's own angel per the Kitzur's count); the stream carries no holy/profane layer — station eleven filed. The seeing-word itself כראת is written lean, no vav (DB-checked), against the full form the Kitzur's citation carries.

THE SCRIBAL DOTS HIT THE EXACT HARD CASE OF THE CHAIN'S OWN RULE, AND OUR INK PROVES IT. The rule is that where the dots are the majority you expound the dots, and where the letters are the majority you expound the letters. At this kiss the chain says the two are EQUAL - which is why it records BOTH readings and settles neither: either he kissed wholeheartedly, or he came to bite and the neck turned to marble, and 'they wept' becomes one weeping over his neck and the other over his teeth. Machine-checked: the word carries SIX consonants and SIX upper dots, exactly equal. Of the five dotted passages in Genesis, three are fully dotted and two only partially - so the precondition the chain claims for this verse is real and is not general.

check.note: A dotting rule reaching its stated tie-case, verified as an exact six-to-six equality against the corpus.

claim_en: A MISSING BLESSING IS TRACKED UNTIL IT IS DELIVERED TEN CHAPTERS LATER. Grace is heard for eleven of the sons at 33:5 but not for the youngest, who was not yet born - and the chain does not treat the gap as an accident: his grace is deferred and then delivered in his brother's mouth at 43:29. A missing item logged at one verse and closed at another, in a block not yet derived.

check.note: An omission in a blessing logged as outstanding and discharged at a named later verse.

claim_en: THE CHAIN AUDITS A PROMISE THE TEXT NEVER SHOWS BEING KEPT, AND RULES IT PAYABLE RATHER THAN FALSE. He tells his brother he will come to Seir - and R. Abbahu reports the search: we have gone through all of Scripture, and he NEVER went to Seir. Is the truthful one then a deceiver? The answer is a maturity date rather than an excuse: he comes in the future, when saviors ascend Zion to judge the mountain of Esau. An unfulfilled undertaking is audited, confirmed unfulfilled, and reclassified as outstanding.

check.note: An unkept promise verified as unkept across the whole canon and then reclassified as outstanding rather than false.

claim_en: THE GIFT IS ENTERED IN A LEDGER THAT IS EXPECTED TO REVERSE. The tribute given here is read forward: all these gifts the nations are destined to RETURN to the messianic king, the claim carried on a verb read as return rather than bring. And the chain records the etiquette of the transmission - the reading was offered by an unnamed man and adopted by name: as you live, I will say it in your name. A transfer booked as reversible, with the attribution rule recorded beside it.

check.note: A gift booked as a reversible transfer, with the source-attribution etiquette recorded in the same passage.

claim_en: THE PORTION IS USED AS AN OPERATIONS MANUAL, AND THE ONE FAILURE IS RECORDED. Before going to the empire, the chain reports, Rabbeinu would READ THIS PORTION and refuse a Roman escort - and the one time he did not, he had to sell his horse. The narrative is being run as procedure with a logged exception. The four hundred are separately said to have deserted mid-march, and the desertion repaid centuries later when four hundred alone escape on camels.

check.note: A narrative portion used as operational procedure with its single recorded failure, plus a numeric echo centuries later.

claim_en: A GRATITUDE-TO-PLACE LAW IS MINTED, AND A FENCE-BREACH DOCTRINE ENFORCED TWICE BESIDE IT. The camping verb is read three ways - he graced the city's leaders; he set up markets and sold cheap, from which the rule that a man must show gratitude to the place he benefits from; and he entered at dusk and FIXED SABBATH BOUNDARIES, keeping the sabbath before it was given. The section carries a long narrative in which one who breaches the sages' fence is bitten by the serpent of the proverb, enforced against a mocker and then against a sabbatical gleaner - with the quorum rule stated: you were not in the count with us.

check.note: A gratitude obligation to a place derived from a camping verb, beside a fence-breach doctrine enforced in two recorded cases.

claim_en: SELF-AUTHORITY IS PRICED, AND THE TRANSLATION DELETES THE OFFENCE ENTIRELY. Reish Lakish reads the altar's naming as a claim - You are God of the heavenly and I am ruler of the earthly - and Rav Huna rebukes it: even a synagogue beadle does not take authority for himself; TOMORROW YOUR DAUGHTER GOES OUT. The next chapter is thereby priced as the penalty for a self-title. Onkelos does not soften the title but removes it, rendering that he WORSHIPPED ON IT BEFORE the God of Israel. One member prices the offence; the other declines to record one.

check.note: A self-title read as an offence with a named penalty in the next chapter, and deleted outright by the translation.

claim_en: THE COLLECTIVE SHIELD IS DISAGGREGATED AT THE MOMENT OF CRISIS. Two capabilities are claimed - I can pray, I can wage war - but at the sight of the approaching force he DIVIDES THE CHILDREN, and the reason given is that each one's own merit should stand for him. The parable of the fox running out of borrowed arguments carries it: let each placate for itself. Merit is individuated exactly when the aggregate is under test.

check.note: Collective merit deliberately disaggregated to individual accounts at the point of maximum risk.

claim_en: THE THIRD UNCONTESTABLE PURCHASE IS BOUGHT AT THIS VERSE. The doctrine recorded at gen_39 names three places the nations can never call stolen because each was bought on the record; this verse is the third, the burial plot acquired for a hundred units of currency. Onkelos separately identifies the currency as lambs rather than coin. The title doctrine now has all three of its deeds inside the derived corpus.

check.note: The third member of a three-part standing-title doctrine acquired at this verse, completing the set in the derived corpus.

claim_en: THE COMPARISON TO GOD IS REMOVED FROM THE ANTAGONIST'S HONOUR. Where the verse has him say he sees his brother's face as one sees the face of God, Onkelos renders it like the face of THE GREAT ONES - nobles, not the divine. The chain arrives at the same guard from the other side, parsing the word as judges. Two tracks, one refusal: the wicked party's face will not be compared to God's in either member.

check.note: A comparison to the divine removed by the translation and independently reparsed by the midrash, both guarding the same point.
